paragraphs: CAVA Group, Inc. (together with its wholly owned subsidiaries, referred to as the "Company," "CAVA," "we," "us," and "our," unless specified otherwise) was formed as a Delaware corporation in 2015, and prior to that, the first CAVA restaurant opened in 2011 in Bethesda, Maryland. As of December 28, 2025, we operate 439 fast-casual CAVA Restaurants in 28 states and Washington, D.C. The Company's authentic Mediterranean cuisine unites taste and health, with a menu that features chef-curated and customizable bowls and pitas. We centrally produce our dips, spreads, and certain dressing bases for use in our restaurants while also selling our dips, spreads, and prepared dressings in grocery stores.

We believe that our differentiated offerings and broad appeal give us significant opportunity in the Mediterranean and health and wellness food categories. Our guests span age groups, genders, and income brackets with a strong Millennial and a growing Gen Z contingent. The broad appeal of our brand is evidenced by substantial diversity across geographies, formats, dayparts, and channels. We are in the early stages of fulfilling our total restaurant potential, and we believe there is opportunity for more than 1,000 CAVA restaurants in the United States by 2032. We believe we are well positioned to benefit from the following strong and emerging trends:
•Evolving consumer preferences for authentic and ethnic cuisine •Increased focus on health and wellness
•Emphasis on combined quality and convenience
We aim to create an industry-leading, category defining brand rooted in the following strategic pillars:
Expand our Mediterranean Way in Communities Across the Country •Grow our footprint and expand multi-channel access
•Fuel our culinary innovation and communication engine to drive traffic, mix, and check
•Express the essence of our category-defining concept consistently across brand properties
Develop Personal Relationships with Guests, Even as We Scale •Leverage our digital ecosystem to enable more personalized communication with guests
•Deepen our connections with guests and drive increased frequency with our enhanced loyalty offerings
•Create a cohesive physical and digital journey Run Great Restaurants, Every Location, Every Shift
•Streamline and automate preparation to make our restaurants easier to run •Enhance our training and standards to consistently deliver our Mediterranean hospitality
•Leverage technologies to increase automation and improve restaurant operations Operate As a High-Performing Team
•Create a culture of growth and accountability •Use best-in-class data capabilities to unlock powerful, actionable insights

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Our Industry
We operate in a highly competitive industry.

Our future growth depends on our ability to open new restaurants while managing our growth effectively and maintaining our culture, and our historical growth may not be indicative of our future growth.
We may not be able to successfully identify appropriate locations and develop and expand our operations in existing and new markets.
New restaurants may not be profitable, and may negatively affect sales at our existing locations.
Negative changes in guest perception of our brand could negatively impact our business.
Our efforts to market our restaurants and brand may not be successful.
Food safety issues and food-borne illness concerns may harm our business.
If we are unable to maintain or increase prices, our margins may decrease.
The growth of our business depends on our ability to accurately predict guest trends and demand and successfully introduce new menu offerings and improve our existing menu offerings.
We are subject to risks associated with leasing property.
We may not be able to successfully expand our digital and delivery business, which is subject to risks outside of our control.
Our inability or failure to utilize, recognize, respond to, and effectively manage the immediacy of social media could have a material adverse effect on our business.
We may not maintain profitability in the future, especially if we continue to grow at an accelerated rate.
We may not realize the anticipated benefits from past and potential future acquisitions, investments or other strategic initiatives.
Risks Related to Our Manufacturing and Supply Chain
We may not be able to manage our manufacturing and supply chain effectively, which may adversely affect our results of operations.
Our reliance on third parties could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
We may not successfully optimize, operate, and manage our production facilities.
We may experience shortages, delays, or interruptions in the delivery of food items and other products.
We may face increases in food, commodity, energy, and other costs.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors as well as the other information set forth in this Annual Report, including the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and our consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto. If any of the following risks actually occurs, our business, results of operations, prospects, and financial condition may be materially adversely affected. In such case, the trading price of our common stock could decline and you may lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are those that we have identified as material but are not the only risks and uncertainties we face. Our business is also subject to general risks and uncertainties that affect many other companies, including but not limited to overall economic and industry conditions, and additional risks not currently known to us or that we presently deem immaterial may arise or become material and may negatively impact our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations, or the trading price of our common stock. Some statements in this Annual Report, including statements in the following risk factors, constitute forward-looking statements. See "Cautionary Statement Concerning Forward-Looking Statements."

The restaurant industry is highly competitive with respect to, among other things, food quality and presentation, taste preferences, price, brand reputation, digital engagement, service, value, and location. The food manufacturing industry is also highly competitive with respect to, among other things, food quality, taste, functional benefits, nutritional value and ingredients, convenience, brand loyalty and positioning, food variety, product packaging, shelf space, price, and promotional activities. We face significant competition from national, regional, and locally-owned restaurants, including limited service restaurants, particularly within the fast-casual dining and traditional fast-food categories, which offer in-restaurant, carry-out, delivery, and/or catering services. We also compete with grocery stores, convenience stores, meal subscription services, and delivery kitchens, especially those that target guests who seek high-quality food. Our CPG business also faces competition from other producers of dips, spreads, and dressings and other pantry and food items. Further, as we continue to innovate upon our digital strategy and offer more ways to reach our guests through digital channels, such as the CAVA app and the CAVA website, we expect to face increasing competition from food delivery services, which promote a wide variety of restaurant options on their websites.

Many of our competitors have been operating for longer and have a more established market presence than us, and may have better locations, greater name recognition and resources than we do, and, as a result, these competitors may be better positioned to attract guests. Our larger competitors may also be able to take advantage of greater economies of scale than we can and may be better able to limit price increases and/or increase prices to reflect cost pressures and increase their marketing and promotional activity, including through discount strategies. Our competitors may also be able to identify and adapt to changes in guest preferences more quickly than us due to their resources and scale. Changes in guests' tastes, nutritional and dietary trends, methods of ordering, and number and location of competing restaurants often affect the restaurant industry. If we are unable to successfully compete, our sales volume and/or pricing may be subject to downward pressure and we may not be able to increase, or sustain, our growth rate or revenue or remain profitable.

Further, as we expand our geographic presence and develop our digital channels, we anticipate we will face increased competition for channel access. Our competitors will likely grow in number as the Mediterranean food category grows, and we may face the risk that new or existing competitors will mimic our business model, menu offerings, marketing strategies, and overall concept.
Any of the above competitive factors may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Our growth depends on our ability to successfully open new restaurants on a profitable basis. As of December 28, 2025, we owned and operated 439 CAVA Restaurants in 28 states and Washington, D.C. In fiscal 2025, we had 72 Net New CAVA Restaurant Openings. If we are unable to sustain the pace of new restaurant openings, our growth rate may decline. In addition, given the size and scale we have achieved, we expect our growth rates in percentage terms to moderate in the future. Therefore, our historical growth rates are not indicative of our future growth.

In addition to historical information, this discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements based on current expectations that involve risks, uncertainties, and other factors outside the Company's control, as well as assumptions, such as our plans, objectives, expectations, and intentions. Our actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied in the forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including those described under the sections entitled "Cautionary Statement Concerning Forward-Looking Statements" and "Risk Factors" included elsewhere in this Annual Report.

CAVA Group, Inc. (together with its wholly owned subsidiaries, referred to as the "Company," "CAVA," "we," "us," and "our," unless specified otherwise) was formed as a Delaware corporation in 2015, and prior to that, the first CAVA restaurant opened in 2011 in Bethesda, Maryland. The Company is headquartered in Washington, D.C. and, as of December 28, 2025, operates 439 fast-casual CAVA Restaurants in 28 states and Washington, D.C. The Company's authentic Mediterranean cuisine unites taste and health, with a menu that features chef-curated and customizable bowls and pitas. The Company centrally produces dips, spreads, and certain dressing bases for use in its restaurants while also selling its dips, spreads, and prepared dressings in grocery stores.

The Company's operations are conducted as two operating segments: CAVA and CAVA Foods. CAVA includes the operations of all company-owned CAVA restaurants. CAVA Foods includes the production of dips, spreads, and certain dressing bases used in CAVA restaurants as well as sales from the Company's CPG business. These segments were determined on the same basis that the Company's Chief Executive Officer ("CEO"), who is the chief operating decision maker ("CODM"), manages, evaluates, and makes key decisions regarding the business. The CODM does not manage the Company on a consolidated basis.

CAVA Foods is below quantitative thresholds for segment reporting purposes, resulting in CAVA being the Company's one reportable segment for the periods covered by the consolidated financial statements. The Company's CPG operations are included in Other. See Item 8. "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data," Note 13 (Segment Reporting) for more information.

We have continued to see growth in revenue, surpassing $1 billion in revenue in fiscal 2025, due to our Net New CAVA Restaurant openings and Same Restaurant Sales growth. In fiscal 2025, we opened 72 Net New CAVA Restaurants, entering new markets such as Indianapolis, South Florida, Pittsburgh, and Detroit. Our 2025 Net New CAVA Restaurants are trending above $3.0 million in AUV demonstrating strong new restaurant productivity and the portability of the brand across the country. CAVA Restaurant-Level Profit Margin remained strong, while making investments in the business to support culinary innovation, Team Member wages, and menu pricing below inflation.

Future results will be impacted by our ability to continue to successfully expand our restaurant base and navigate challenges and uncertainties such as macroeconomic conditions that may impact guest demand, commodity and wage inflation, and supply chain constraints.

We operate on a 52-week or 53-week fiscal year that ends on the last Sunday of the calendar year. In a 52-week fiscal year, the first fiscal quarter contains sixteen weeks and the second, third and fourth fiscal quarters each contain twelve weeks. In a 53-week fiscal year, the first fiscal quarter contains sixteen weeks, the second and third fiscal quarters each contain twelve weeks, and the fourth fiscal quarter contains thirteen weeks. Fiscal year 2025 and fiscal year 2024 were 52-week periods that ended on December 28, 2025 and December 29, 2024, respectively.

Historically, seasonal factors have caused our revenue to fluctuate from quarter to quarter. Our revenue per restaurant is typically lower in the first and fourth fiscal quarters due to reduced traffic as a result of colder temperatures and the holiday season.

As a result of these factors and the differences among our fiscal quarters, our quarterly operating results and Same Restaurant Sales, as well as other key performance measures, may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and our results for any one quarter are not indicative of any other quarter.

In assessing the performance of our business, in addition to considering a variety of measures in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ("GAAP"), our management team also considers a variety of other key performance measures, including non-GAAP measures. The key performance measures used by our management for determining how our business is performing are detailed below.

We believe that these key performance measures provide useful information to users of our financial statements in understanding and evaluating our results of operations in the same manner as our management team. paragraphs: CAVA Group, Inc.（與其全資子公司合稱為「本公司」、「CAVA」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」，除非另有說明）於2015年成立為特拉華州公司，而在那之前，第一家CAVA餐廳於2011年在馬裏蘭州貝塞斯達開幕。截至2025年12月28日，我們在28個州及華盛頓特區經營439家快速餐飲CAVA餐廳。本公司的正宗地中海料理結合美味與健康，其菜單特色為主廚策劃且可客製化的碗裝與皮塔包。我們中央製造我們的蘸醬、醬料及部分調味基底，供應給我們的餐廳，同時也將我們的蘸醬、醬料及預備好的調味品銷售至超市。

我們認為，我們的差異化產品與廣泛的吸引力，使我們在地中海及健康與 wellness 食品類別中擁有顯著的成長機會。我們的顧客年齡層、性別及收入層級皆涵蓋，其中以千禧世代為主，且Z世代的顧客正在成長。我們品牌的廣泛吸引力，從地理區域、店鋪形式、用餐時段及通路的多樣性可見一斑。我們目前處於實現總體餐廳潛力的初期階段，我們認為到2032年，美國將有機會開設超過1,000家CAVA餐廳。我們認為我們處於有利位置，可受益於以下強勁且興起的趨勢：
•消費者對正宗及民族料理的偏好逐漸改變 •對健康與 wellness 的關注增加
•強調品質與便利性的結合
我們旨在建立一個行業領先、定義類別的品牌，根植於以下戰略支柱：
擴展我們的地中海方式於全美各社區 •擴大我們的據點並拓展多通路接觸
•推動我們的料理創新與溝通引擎，以提升人流量、銷售組合與消費金額
•在品牌各項屬性中，一致地表達我們定義類別的概念本質
發展與顧客的個人關係，即使我們規模擴張 • 利用我們的數位生態系統，以實現與顧客更為個性化的溝通
• 深化與顧客的連結，並推動更高的消費頻率，透過我們加強的忠誠度方案
• 建立一致的實體與數位體驗 運營優秀的餐廳，每個據點、每個班次
• 簡化並自動化準備流程，使我們的餐廳更容易經營 • 提升我們的培訓與標準，以一致地提供我們的地中海式款待
• 利用科技提高自動化程度，並改善餐廳營運 營運為高績效團隊
• 建立成長與責任的文化 • 利用最佳等級的數據能力，以解鎖強大且具行動力的見解

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們經審計之合併財務報表及其相關附註，包含於本年度報告第 8 項「財務報表與補充資料」中一併閱讀。有關 2024 年 12 月 29 日財務年度與 2023 年 12 月 31 日財務年度之比較，請參閱本年度報告第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」，該部分為 2024 年 12 月 29 日財務年度之 10-K 報告，於 2025 年 2 月 26 日向 SEC 提交。除歷史資訊外，本討論與分析包含基於目前預期之展望性陳述，涉及風險、不確定性及其他非本公司所能控制之因素，以及假設，例如我們的計畫、目標、預期與意圖。我們實際結果可能因多種因素而與展望性陳述所表達或暗示者有重大差異，包括於本年度報告其他部分所列之「對展望性陳述之警示聲明」及「風險因素」等節目所描述之因素。

CAVA Group, Inc.（與其全資子公司合稱為「本公司」、「CAVA」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們」，除非另有說明）於 2015 年成立為德拉瓦州公司，而在那之前，第一家 CAVA 餐廳於 2011 年在馬裏蘭州貝塞斯達開幕。本公司總部設於華盛頓特區，截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，於 28 個州及華盛頓特區運作 439 家快速餐飲 CAVA 餐廳。本公司提供正宗的地中海料理，結合美味與健康，其菜單特色為主廚策劃且可客製化的碗裝與皮塔包。本公司於中央生產蘸醬、醬料及部分調味基底，供應於其餐廳，同時亦於超級市場販售其蘸醬、醬料及預備調味料。
本公司營運分為兩個營運分部：CAVA 與 CAVA Foods。CAVA 包含所有本公司所有之 CAVA 餐廳營運。CAVA Foods 包含用於 CAVA 餐廳之蘸醬、醬料及部分調味基底之生產，以及本公司 CPG 事業之銷售。這些分部係根據本公司執行長（「CEO」），為主要營運決策者（「CODM」）所管理、評估及做出關鍵決策之基礎所決定。CODM 並未以合併基礎管理本公司。
CAVA Foods 在分部報告之量化門檻以下，因此本公司於合併財務報表所涵蓋期間，僅有 CAVA 為應報告分部。本公司 CPG 事業包含於其他項目。詳見第 8 項「財務報表與補充資料」，附註 13（分部報告）以取得更多資訊。

我們持續觀察到營收成長，於財務年度 2025 超過 10 億美元營收，係因我們的淨新增 CAVA 餐廳開幕與同店銷售成長。於財務年度 2025，我們開幕 72 家淨新增 CAVA 餐廳，進駐新市場，如印第安那波利斯、南佛羅裏達、匹茲堡與底特律。我們 2025 年淨新增 CAVA 餐廳之平均單店價值超過 300 萬美元，顯示強勁的新餐廳生產力與品牌在全國的可移植性。CAVA 餐廳層面的毛利率維持強勁，同時對業務進行投資，以支持廚藝創新、員工工資與菜單價格低於通貨膨脹。
未來結果將受我們持續成功擴張餐廳基礎與應對挑戰與不確定性之能力影響，例如總體經濟條件可能影響顧客需求、原物料與工資通貨膨脹，以及供應鏈限制。

我們採用 52 週或 53 週財務年度，於曆年最後一個星期日結束。在 52 週財務年度中，第一財季包含 16 週，第二、第三及第四財季各包含 12 週。在 53 週財務年度中，第一財季包含 16 週，第二及第三財季各包含 12 週，第四財季包含 13 週。財務年度 2025 與財務年度 2024 均為 52 週期間，分別於 2025 年 12 月 28 日與 2024 年 12 月 29 日結束。
歷來，季節性因素導致我們營收於各季度間波動。我們每家餐廳之營收通常在第一及第四財季較低，因較低的客流量，係因較低溫度與節日季節所致。
因這些因素以及我們的會計年度各季之間的差異，我們的每季營運結果及同店銷售額，以及其他關鍵績效指標，可能從一季到另一季大幅波動，任何一季的結果並不能代表其他季的結果。
在評估我們業務的表現時，除了依照美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）考量多種衡量指標外，我們的管理團隊也會考量多種其他關鍵績效指標，包括非GAAP指標。我們管理團隊用來判斷業務表現的關鍵績效指標詳列於下。

我們認為這些關鍵績效指標能為財務報表的使用者提供有用的資訊，以相同的方式理解與評估我們的營運結果。這些關鍵績效指標的呈現，包括調整後的營業現金流（Adjusted EBITDA）、調整後的營業現金流率（Adjusted EBITDA margin）、調整後淨收入（Adjusted Net Income）及調整後淨收入率（Adjusted Net Income margin），這些為非GAAP財務指標，並非用來孤立考量，或取代、優於依照GAAP準則編製與呈現的財務資訊。請參閱下方的"非GAAP財務指標"部分。
以下表格列示我們在所指會計年度的關鍵績效指標：

headings: 與本公司業務及產業相關之風險
本公司經營於一高度競爭之產業。
本公司未來之成長取決於本公司能否開設新餐廳同時有效管理成長並維持本公司文化，且本公司歷史成長可能無法反映本公司未來成長。
本公司可能無法成功識別適當之位置並發展及擴展本公司業務於現有及新市場。
新餐廳可能無法獲利，且可能對本公司現有場地之銷售造成負面影響。
顧客對本公司品牌之負面觀感可能對本公司業務造成負面影響。
本公司行銷餐廳及品牌之努力可能無法成功。
食品安全問題及食源性疾病之擔憂可能損害本公司業務
若我們無法維持或提高價格，我們的毛利率可能會下降。
我們業務的成長取決於我們能否準確預測顧客趨勢與需求，並成功推出新餐點及改善現有餐點。
我們面臨與租賃不動產相關之風險。
我們可能無法成功擴展數位與外送業務，而此業務面臨許多我們無法控制的風險。
我們若無法有效運用、辨識、回應並管理社交媒體的即時性，可能會對我們業務造成重大不利影響。
我們未來可能無法維持獲利能力，特別是在我們持續以加速速度成長的情況下。
我們可能無法實現過去或未來潛在之併購、投資或其他戰略計畫預期的效益。
與我們製造與供應鏈相關之風險
我們可能無法有效管理製造與供應鏈，這可能會對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
我們對第三方的依賴可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們可能無法成功優化、運作及管理生產設施。
我們可能面臨食品項、其他產品的供應短缺、延遲或交付中斷的情況。
我們可能面臨食品、商品、能源及其他成本的增加。
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考慮下列風險因素，以及本年度報告中所載的其他資訊，包括標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」的章節，以及我們的合併財務報表及其相關附註。若上述任何風險因素實際發生，將可能對我們的業務、營運結果、前景及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。在此情況下，我們的普通股交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所描述的風險與不確定性，是我們已識別為重大的風險與不確定性，但並非我們所面臨的唯一風險與不確定性。我們的業務亦受到影響許多其他公司的普遍風險與不確定性，包括但不限於總體經濟與產業條件，以及目前尚未為我們所知或目前認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，這些風險與不確定性可能後續出現或變得重要，並可能對我們的業務、聲譽、財務狀況、營運結果或普通股交易價格造成負面影響。本年度報告中的一些陳述，包括下列風險因素中的陳述，屬於前瞻性陳述。請參閱「關於前瞻性陳述的警示聲明。」

餐飲業在食品品質與呈現、口味偏好、價格、品牌聲譽、數位參與、服務、價值與位置等方面具有高度競爭性。食品製造業在食品品質、口味、功能性好處、營養價值與成分、便利性、品牌忠誠度與定位、食品種類、產品包裝、架位空間、價格與促銷活動等方面亦具有高度競爭性。我們面臨來自全國性、區域性及地方性餐廳的激烈競爭，包括有限服務餐廳，特別是在快速餐飲與傳統速食類別中，這些餐廳提供堂食、外帶、外送與/或餐飲服務。我們也與超市、便利商店、餐點訂閱服務與外送廚房競爭，尤其是那些針對尋求高品質食品的顧客。我們的消費品業務亦面臨來自其他生產調料、醬料與調味品及其他廚房用品製造商的競爭。此外，隨著我們持續創新數位策略並透過數位通路提供更多方式來接觸顧客，例如CAVA應用程式與CAVA網站，我們預期將面臨來自食品外送服務的競爭增加，這些服務在他們網站上促銷多種餐廳選項。

我們的許多競爭對手已經營運較久，且市場佔有率較我們更為成熟，可能擁有更佳的店面位置、更高的品牌知名度與資源，因此這些競爭對手可能更有能力吸引顧客。我們的較大規模競爭對手可能更能利用規模經濟，並更有效地限制價格上漲或提高價格以反映成本壓力，並增加其行銷與促銷活動，包括透過折扣策略。競爭對手也可能因資源與規模較我們更優而更能迅速識別並適應顧客偏好變化。顧客的口味、營養與飲食趨勢、點餐方式以及競爭餐廳的數量與位置，經常影響餐飲業。若我們無法成功競爭，我們的銷售量與/或價格可能面臨下行壓力，我們可能無法增加或維持我們的成長率或營收，或維持盈利。
此外，隨著我們擴展地理存在並發展數位通路，我們預期將面臨更多競爭以取得通路。隨著地中海美食類別成長，競爭對手的數量將很可能增加，我們可能面臨新興或現有競爭對手模仿我們的商業模式、餐點選項、行銷策略與整體概念的風險。
上述任何競爭因素可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。
我們的成長取決於我們能否以獲利方式成功開設新餐廳。截至2025年12月28日，我們擁有並營運439間CAVA餐廳，分佈於28個州與華盛頓特區。在2025會計年度，我們有72間淨新增CAVA餐廳開幕。若我們無法維持新餐廳開幕的速度，我們的成長率可能下降。此外，考慮到我們已達成的規模與規模，我們預期未來以百分比計算的成長率將趨緩。因此，我們的歷史成長率並不能代表我們未來的成長。
